Process_Text.original: All samples were fabricated using an in-house developed 3-axis L-DED system equipped with a 1 kW fibre laser (IPG Photonics Corporation). The wavelength of the laser is 1070 nm, and its nominal beam size is 1 mm. Cuboid samples measuring 52 mm × 6 mm × 6 mm (L × W × H) were printed using the L-DED system, before tensile coupons were cut out using wire electrical discharge machining (EDM). Before each tensile test, the gauge sections of the coupons were mechanically polished down to a surface roughness of 1.78 ± 0.137 μm.
Process_Text.simplified: L-DED printing of homogeneous 316L using 1 kW fibre laser, followed by EDM cutting and mechanical polishing.

Structure_Text.original: In the homogenous 316L steel, the only phase presented is the γ phase. The 316L regions show cellular structures with various morphologies as a result of constitutional supercooling. Coarser grains are found on the 316L side. All samples show a porosity <0.1% and are thus considered to be fully dense. Density > 99.9%.
Structure_Text.simplified: Homogeneous 316L: single-phase austenite (γ, FCC), cellular solidification structures, porosity <0.1%.

Process_Text.original: The samples are designed to have a laminated configuration along the transverse direction (TD). The control of lamella width was achieved leveraging an inverse process parameter optimization framework. Laser power, scan speed, and powder feed rate are set at 450 W, 4 mm/s, and 0.175 g/min. Two hoppers storing 316L and PH17-4 powders were alternatively turned on and off, with 15 s pause between each alternation for the powder stream to stabilize. Two hatch spacings: 0.70 mm and 0.81 mm.
Process_Text.simplified: L-DED printing of alternating 316L/PH17-4 lamellae via dual-hopper powder switching with 15s pause, two sub-configurations using hatch spacings 0.70 mm and 0.81 mm respectively, followed by EDM cutting and mechanical polishing.

Structure_Text.original: The samples are comprised of mainly two phases, i.e., face centered cubic (FCC) and body centered cubic (BCC), corresponding to 316L and PH17-4, respectively. No new phase is observed for the HS samples. Good bonding with clear boundaries is observed between the 316L and PH17-4 regions. Clear boundaries between the two materials with minimal element diffusion. No precipitates identified in PH17-4 or at the boundary.
Structure_Text.simplified: Bi-metallic HS with alternating 316L (FCC austenite) and PH17-4 (BCC martensite) lamellae, coherent interface with Kurdjumov-Sachs orientation relationship, no new phases or precipitates.

Main_Phase.Note: FCC in 316L regions, BCC in PH17-4 regions; XRD shows superposition of both phases

Interface_Features.Note: Misfit < 5%, classified as coherent interface. No precipitates at interface.

Saturation_Stress_MPa.Note: From Kocks-Mecking fit of work hardening stage III (Table 4)

Process_Text.original: Numerical finite element analysis (FEA) was implemented to study the stress and strain fields and the deformation modes of the various HS samples. Three-dimensional CAD models were created replicating the geometrical signatures of the tested HS samples. The FEA simulations were performed using the commercial software ABAQUS with an explicit solver.
Process_Text.simplified: 3D FEA using ABAQUS explicit solver to simulate tensile deformation of HS samples.
